title: Polynomial extension data for a finite inclusion over a normal Noetherian domain
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative domains. Assume $A$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in C$ generate $C$ as an $A$-module via $\varphi$, meaning every $c\in C$ equals $\sum_{j=1}^r\varphi(a_j)c_j$ for some $a_j\in A$. For every integer $n\ge0$ put $A_n=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $C_n=C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $\varphi_n:A_n\to C_n$ apply $\varphi$ to coefficients and fix the variables. Then $\varphi_n$ is injective, $A_n$ is a Noetherian normal domain, and $C_n$ is a domain. The constant polynomials $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ generate $C_n$ as an $A_n$-module via $\varphi_n$, and also as an $A_n$-algebra. Moreover $\varphi_n$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and integral: every element of $C_n$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi_n(A_n)$. The case $n=0$ is included.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation (3); Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral. The coefficientwise map and unchanged module generators are the elementary polynomial calculation in the finite affine specialization of more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open.

proof.text: By the finite monomial description in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], the coefficient of $t^\alpha$ in $\varphi_n(f)$ is $\varphi(f_\alpha)$. Thus $\varphi_n(f)=\varphi_n(g)$ implies $\varphi(f_\alpha)=\varphi(g_\alpha)$ for each $\alpha$, hence $f_\alpha=g_\alpha$ by injectivity of $\varphi$, and $f=g$. Coefficientwise addition and the finite convolution formula for multiplication also show that this is the stated ring homomorphism.

source.place: Finite monomial calculation; coefficient map used in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32 (lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open).

proof.text: Regrouping $t^{(\alpha,k)}$ as $t^\alpha t_{m+1}^k$ identifies $R[t_1,\ldots,t_{m+1}]$ with $R[t_1,\ldots,t_m][t_{m+1}]$: the inverse expands each coefficient, and addition and multiplication agree by finite sums. For a domain $D$, nonzero polynomials of degrees $a,b$ have product coefficient at degree $a+b$ equal to the product of their nonzero leading coefficients; thus $D[T]$ is a domain. Induction starting at $C_0=C$ gives that $C_n$ is a domain. Starting at the normal domain $A_0=A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] at each induction step under this same identification to conclude that every $A_n$ is a normal domain.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal; induction by regrouping monomials.

proof.text: The $n$ variables generate $A_n$ as an $A$-algebra: each polynomial is a finite sum of coefficient multiples of products of the variables. Equivalently it is the polynomial algebra in these variables modulo the zero ideal. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applied to $A\to A_n$ proves that $A_n$ is Noetherian.

For $f=\sum_{\alpha\in S}b_\alpha t^\alpha\in C_n$, choose $a_{\alpha j}\in A$ with $b_\alpha=\sum_{j=1}^r\varphi(a_{\alpha j})c_j$, for each member of the finite support $S$. Put $p_j=\sum_{\alpha\in S}a_{\alpha j}t^\alpha\in A_n$. Distributing finite sums gives $f=\sum_{j=1}^r\varphi_n(p_j)c_j$. These are exactly the original constant generators, so they span $C_n$ as an $A_n$-module. Every $A_n$-subalgebra containing them contains these sums; hence they also generate $C_n$ as an $A_n$-algebra. Evaluation $A_n[u_1,\ldots,u_r]\to C_n$, $u_j\mapsto c_j$, is therefore surjective, exhibiting finite type. For $n=0$ the only monomial is $1$ and the formula is precisely the given spanning hypothesis.

source.place: Elementary coefficient expansion in the finite affine case of more-morphisms.tex Tag 0F32, lemma-quasi-finite-Noetherian-universally-open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] to the finite-type $A_n$-algebra $C_n$ from step 4, using Noetherianity of $A_n$ from step 3. This gives finite presentation of the given coefficient map $\varphi_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to the finite $A_n$-module $C_n$ from step 4: each element is a root of a monic polynomial over the image of $A_n$. Both applications include $n=0$.
